rationale: Builds directly on the current best late-skip recurrent-tail baseline and composes it with the closest traversal miss: keep the winning trimmed late decoder skips, but run the two recurrent tail blocks in reverse order so the last block settles first before the earlier tail block re-edits the state. This is a compile-stable traversal-only change with essentially unchanged byte budget and step structure, which fits the underexplored traversal category without spending the run on another minor optimizer sweep.
title: Reverse-Order Tail Recurrence On Tail-Focused Late Decoder Skips
